plan.summary: This 4-week block starts the 12-week off-camp build for boxing with simple bodyweight strength, low-impact power, trunk work, and a short conditioning finisher. Week 1 is used to establish baseline rep performance on the main bodyweight strength lifts so later blocks can progress from clear starting numbers. With only 1 S&C session per week and a bodyweight-only setup, the plan keeps the highest-value work first, manages fatigue, and uses conditioning that supports boxing without burying recovery.

phaseOverview.label: Building
phaseOverview.focus: Build basic full-body strength, landing mechanics, trunk stiffness, and repeatable conditioning with simple bodyweight work.

phaseOverview.label: Intensifying
phaseOverview.focus: Progress harder bodyweight variations and raise power and conditioning density while keeping technique clean.

phaseOverview.label: Expressing
phaseOverview.focus: Keep strength, sharpen speed and explosiveness, and carry the work into more fight-relevant output without excess fatigue.

exercises.name: 1a. Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Reset between reps. Jump fast and land quietly with good balance.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if you want a simpler jump with less coordination demand.

substitutionOptions.name: Low Pogo Jumps
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if jump tolerance is low and you need the lowest-impact option.

exercises.name: 1b. Plyo Push-Up to Hands-Elevated Surface
exercises.notes: Explode off the support and catch softly. Use a wall, bench, or sturdy surface that lets every rep stay sharp.

substitutionOptions.name: Fast Incline Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if leaving the surface is too advanced right now.

exercises.name: 2. Push-Up
exercises.reps: AMRAP stopping at clean form break
exercises.notes: This is your baseline test for future progress. Warm up with a few easy sets, then do one hard top set and stop as soon as body line or range slips.

strengthAssessment.prompt: Warm up progressively, then perform one hard top set of clean push-ups and stop at the first real form break. Log the reps so the app can set your baseline for later progress.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track your best clean set and aim to beat it over time without shortening range.

substitutionOptions.name: Hands-Elevated Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if floor push-ups are not yet clean for multiple reps.

exercises.name: 3. Split Squat
exercises.reps: AMRAP each side stopping at clean form break
exercises.notes: This is your baseline lower-body strength test. Use a full controlled range and keep the torso tall. Match left and right side effort.

strengthAssessment.prompt: Warm up progressively, then perform one hard top set per side with clean split squats. Log the reps for each leg so the app can set your baseline for later progress.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track the best clean rep count on each leg and build balance between sides.

substitutionOptions.name: Reverse Lunge
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if split squat setup is uncomfortable or balance is easier with a step back.

exercises.name: 4a. Table Row or Towel Row
exercises.notes: Use a setup that feels secure. Pull the chest toward the hands and keep the body rigid. Stop 1-2 reps before form breaks.

substitutionOptions.name: Doorframe Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use only if the setup is stable and safe.

substitutionOptions.name: Backpack Bent-Over Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if you can load a backpack and need a safer home option.

exercises.name: 4b. Forearm Plank
exercises.notes: Brace hard, squeeze glutes, and keep ribs down. End the set if the lower back starts sagging.

substitutionOptions.name: RKC Plank
substitutionOptions.notes: Use for a shorter but harder brace.

substitutionOptions.name: Hollow Body Hold
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if you want a stronger anterior trunk challenge.

exercises.name: 5. Shadowboxing Conditioning
exercises.notes: Stay relaxed and sharp. Keep the feet active and the hands moving with clean technique, not sloppy volume.

endurancePrescription.rest: 1 minute easy walk and nasal breathing
